questions.def: Cleft sentences emphasize information; 'it + be + emphasized part + that/who'.
questions.question: It was ___ that I saw yesterday.

questions.def: 'That' or 'who/which' introduces the clause in a cleft sentence.
questions.question: It was the rain ___ made us stay inside.

questions.def: 'That' connects the emphasized part to the rest of the sentence.
questions.question: It was pizza ___ he wanted.

questions.def: The subject of the relative clause after 'who' is 'my sister'.
questions.question: It was ___ who helped me.

questions.def: The time expression 'yesterday' is placed directly after 'was'.
questions.question: It was ___ yesterday that I finished the project.

questions.def: 'Who made' correctly completes the cleft sentence structure.
questions.question: It was her ___ that cake.

questions.def: Cleft sentences emphasize the information placed after 'it is'.
questions.question: It is ___ that I want to learn.

questions.def: The phrase 'my friends who went' correctly emphasizes who went.
questions.question: It was ___ to the party.

questions.def: 'That' connects the emphasized part, and 'bought' is past tense.
questions.question: It was this car ___ he ___.

questions.def: Cleft sentences emphasize specific information; 'a holiday' is appropriate.
questions.question: It was ___ I needed.

questions.def: 'That' correctly introduces the relative clause modifying 'music'.
questions.question: It is ___ makes me happy.

questions.def: 'That' introduces the clause, and 'saw' is the past tense verb.
questions.question: It was her ___ he ___ at the party.

questions.def: Cleft sentences emphasize the lost item; 'my keys' is appropriate.
questions.question: It was ___ that I lost.

questions.def: 'Sarah who wrote' is the correct structure for this cleft sentence.
questions.question: It was ___ the report.

questions.def: 'Who helped' is correct form, 'the' is correct article.
questions.question: It was John ___ me with ___ homework.

questions.def: Cleft sentences emphasize what was broken, 'the vase'.
questions.question: It was ___ that he broke.

questions.def: 'My brother who' is the correct combination for this cleft sentence.
questions.question: It was ___ told me the news.

questions.def: 'That' refers to the book. 'found' is past tense.
questions.question: It was this book ___ I ___ interesting.

questions.def: Cleft sentences highlight what is needed; 'some rest' is correct.
questions.question: It is ___ I need right now.

questions.def: 'Their friends who' is grammatically correct in this cleft sentence.
questions.question: It was ___ helped them.

questions.def: 'Who organized' refers to Maria; 'organized' is past tense.
questions.question: It was Maria ___ the party.

questions.def: Cleft sentences emphasize reason; 'the traffic' is most appropriate.
questions.question: It was ___ she was late.

questions.def: 'The mechanic who' correctly identifies the person in the sentence.
questions.question: It was ___ fixed the car.

questions.def: Use 'who' when referring to a person as the subject.
questions.question: It was John ___ broke the window.

questions.def: 'That' introduces the clause emphasizing 'music'.
questions.question: It is the music ___ I love about this movie.

questions.def: The past tense form of 'read' is also 'read'.
questions.question: It was this book that I ___ last night.

questions.def: Use 'that' or 'which' for objects in cleft sentences.
questions.question: It wasn't the car ___ was stolen.

questions.def: 'That' connects the reason to the result in a cleft sentence.
questions.question: It is because I am tired ___ I can't go out.

questions.def: 'Cooks' agrees with the singular subject 'mother'.
questions.question: It is my mother who ___ dinner every night.

questions.def: 'That' introduces the clause, focusing on the location.
questions.question: It was in Paris ___ I met her.
